detail: baseline read from the COMMITTED reviews/MAPGEN-026/summary.csv - 75,629 rows, Spain 5,431, Portugal 26, 318 hexes with no row
5,431 Spanish TERRESTRIAL_HEX rows, identical to MAPGEN-026, and the revision log records no row moving to Spain

68 rows changed in this stage, every one written to the revision log with its before and after state and all of them UNRESOLVED before; MAPGEN-014's 401 earlier revisions are still there, appended to rather than replaced
345 hexes audited, covering all 318 MAPGEN-026 left unaddressed, each with its safe-interior, frontier-band, special-case and mixed-land status and a candidate fragment id
9 fragments CONTROLLED and all 345 registered and promoted; MAPGEN-026 produced none in Iberia
no TERRESTRIAL_HEX row addresses a non-terrestrial hex, and no fragment's parent hex carries a hex row: the OCEAN hex is still not owned
139 hexes hold land of more than one physical component, the worst 103; the other components' 18.9 km2 is measured and left unowned
the plate's ROYAUME DE ALGARVE lettering is recorded as a foreign engraving convention, not as evidence about an actor in either direction
8 axes examined against the crown's own printed legislation, an archival finding aid for the Tavira corregedoria, and a University of Lisbon study
PART_OF_POL_PORTUGAL: no axis supports a separate actor, and no new polity was created. The Naples/Sicily comparison is recorded on the decision row

Gaceta de Madrid num. 30 of 27 July 1756, five days before the snapshot: the King appoints an oidor to the Chancilleria de Granada and a fiscal to the Consejo de Navarra. The 3 August assertion is kept

four acts of 1756 dated before the snapshot in the crown's own compilation, including the Decreto de 15 de Junho ordering the Desembargo do Paco to publish by edict in every town of the Province of Alentejo. The Douro alvara is kept
3 files acquired from the Universidade de Coimbra Biblioteca Geral Digital, with catalogue id, date, cartographer, dimensions, sha256 and acquisition time recorded
both sheets are CC BY 4.0 open access, so commercial reuse is not impeded; the rasters are gitignored and only their hashes are committed

the Vaugondy sheet is of the Sanson/Jaillot/Vaugondy family and Le Rouge's own lineage is NOT ESTABLISHED, so their relation is UNRESOLVED in both directions and neither counts as independent corroboration of the other

the 1762 sheet post-dates the snapshot and the Spanish invasion of Portugal ran May-November 1762; the continuity argument and the campaign-line risk are both recorded, and nothing in production relies on either

3 points were identified to calibrate a SEARCH window and every one is marked ineligible as a control point. No Vaugondy GCP exists, because the plate draws towns as vignettes and a vignette has no defensible single point - the reason MAPGEN-026 rejected Cuenca and Cordoba
no FIT/MODEL_SELECTION/BLIND split was manufactured for the Vaugondy sheets, because no model was fitted; the work is handed to MAPGEN-028 with its reason
MAPGEN-026's wording is corrected: the model-selection holdout chose POLYNOMIAL_2 and is therefore NOT statistically blind. The four sets are reported separately
the erosion uses ALL_NONFIT p95 = 34.61 km, the more conservative of the two candidates (the blind p95 is 23.30 km on 5 points in 2 quadrants)
the transform this production rests on is still the MAPGEN-026 POLYNOMIAL_2, and its Jacobian over the whole face does not fold
the uncertainty is UNCHANGED from MAPGEN-026 because no new georeference was made; Portugal's recovery came from evidence, and the report says so
no frontier geometry was digitised from the Vaugondy sheets, because a trace from an ungeoreferenced plate cannot be placed on the ground
the Le Rouge / Vaugondy frontier comparison is recorded as NOT PERFORMED with its reason, rather than left unmentioned
no boundary was averaged between sources; only one source's geometry is in force and the other is recorded as unused
v2 contains all of v1, overlaps Spain's safe interior by 0.0 km2, and grows from 1,643 to 5,480 km2 (projected)
Gibraltar, Andorra, Llivia, Olivenza, the Couto Misto and Ceuta are still each withheld inside one uncertainty radius
the Algarve cell is owned by Portugal and removed from the withheld list, because the audit said so and only because it said so
5,554 CONTROLLED hexes, every one with all of its land inside a single crown's safe interior, measured on the exact hex-land intersection
no hex carrying authorised safe coastal land is left NOT_PRODUCED any more; every fragment is either CONTROLLED or explicitly UNRESOLVED
hex land is measured with land_in_hexes(), which unions the tile intersections inside each hex before measuring
no hex reports more land than a hex can hold (31.18 km2 projected); a naive sum over overlapping cache tiles would show exactly that, and MAPGEN-024 once did
the promotion id is deterministic on the candidate hash, so a re-run inserts nothing; the log carries one MAPGEN-027 entry
every one of the 76,576 canonical rows has a provenance row except the three MAPGEN-008 Kanto foundation rows, which predate the provenance table and are named rather than waved through
Portugal stays TERRITORY_PARTIAL and the coverage note says plainly that it is still thin and why
the scenario preview was re-rendered; the closeup and the Europe map are regenerated and no unrecovered gap hex is drawn
Great Britain 20,310 and Ireland 7,520 hexes, unchanged since MAPGEN-021
Sicily 1,305 and Sardinia 1,308 hexes, unchanged since MAPGEN-022
Iceland 18,341 and Malta/Gozo 15 hexes, unchanged since MAPGEN-023
Spain 5,431 hexes, identical to the 5,431 MAPGEN-026 committed
Brandenburg still holds nothing: MAPGEN-020 left it un-produced and this stage did not change that
Electoral Saxony 695 hexes, unchanged since MAPGEN-015
the canonical Europe grid is still 1,885,422 hexes; no physical geography was touched
the claim table still holds exactly the one MAPGEN-008 Kanto row; this stage created none
